focus: Contractions 've /v/ (I've, we've) and 's /z/ (she's been) · 'been' /biːn/ vs 'bin' /bɪn/ · 'ever/never' stress · weak 'have' /həv/ in questions · linking 'have you ever'
focus_ar: الاختصارات 've و 's، و 'been' مقابل 'bin'، ونبر ever/never، و 'have' الخفيفة في السؤال
arabic_challenge: The present perfect has no direct Arabic equivalent, and its contracted auxiliaries ('I've', 'she's') are often expanded or dropped. 'Been' is frequently shortened to 'bin', and the /v/ of 'have/'ve' is hard because Arabic has no /v/.

isolation.instructions: 'Have' contracts to 've = a single /v/ on the pronoun: I've /aɪv/, we've /wiːv/, they've /ðeɪv/, you've /juːv/. Feel the top teeth touch the bottom lip and buzz.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'have' بتتقلّص لـ 've = /v/ على الضمير: I've، we've، they've. الأسنان العليا على الشفة السفلى مع طنين.

daily_drills.record_this: I've been to Cairo many times. We've seen that film before, but they've never tried Egyptian food.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'I've been'. Is there a clear /v/ buzz, with teeth touching lip?

isolation.instructions: With he/she/it, 'has' contracts to 's = /z/: she's been, he's done, it's been. Careful: 's can be 'is' OR 'has' — the past participle after it tells you it's 'has' (she's been = she HAS been).
isolation.instructions_ar: مع he/she/it تتقلّص 'has' لـ 's = /z/: she's been. انتبه: 's ممكن 'is' أو 'has' — التصريف الثالث بعدها يدل إنها 'has'.

daily_drills.record_this: She's been to London twice. He's already done his homework, and it's rained all day, so she's decided to stay home.
daily_drills.self_check: In 'she's been', can you tell it means 'she HAS been' from the participle 'been'?

isolation.instructions: In careful speech 'been' is /biːn/ with a long /iː/. Do not shorten it to 'bin' /bɪn/ (a rubbish bin). The present perfect leans on this word, so keep the vowel long.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'been' في الكلام المتأني /biːn/ بحرف علة طويل. متقصّرهاش لـ 'bin' /bɪn/ (سلة). المضارع التام بيعتمد عليها.

sentence_practice: Have you ever been to Alexandria?
daily_drills.record_this: Have you ever been to Alexandria? I've been there twice, and it's beautiful. My sister has never been abroad, but she's been to many cities in Egypt.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'been'. Is the vowel long like 'bean', not short like 'bin'?

isolation.instructions: 'Ever' and 'never' carry meaning, so they are stressed: 'Have you EVER…?', 'I've NEVER…'. EV-er and NEV-er both stress the first syllable. Do not swallow them.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'ever' و 'never' بيحملوا معنى فبيتنبروا: 'Have you EVER…?'. النبر على المقطع الأول في الاتنين.

daily_drills.record_this: Have you ever eaten sushi? I've never tried it, but I've always wanted to. My friend has just returned from Japan, and she's never been so happy.
daily_drills.self_check: Are 'EVER' and 'NEVER' clearly stressed on the first syllable and easy to hear?

isolation.instructions: In questions, 'have' is weak: /həv/ or /əv/. 'Have you ever been…?' flows as 'həv-you-EV-er-BEEN'. The stress lands on 'ever' and the participle, not on 'have'.
isolation.instructions_ar: في السؤال 'have' خفيفة: /həv/. 'Have you ever been…?' → həv-you-EV-er-BEEN. النبر على ever والتصريف الثالث.

sentence_practice: Have you ever been to another country?
Has she ever tried Egyptian food?
daily_drills.record_this: Have you ever been to another country? Have you seen this new film? Has your sister ever tried Egyptian food? I've done all three, but you haven't yet.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'Have you ever been?' as one flow. Does 'have' stay weak, with stress on 'ever' and 'been'?

challenge_sentences: Have you ever been to Alexandria?
I've been there but I've never seen the sea in winter.
She's just finished and he's already gone.
We've always wanted to travel abroad.
daily_drills.record_this: Have you ever been to Alexandria? I've been there twice, but I've never seen the sea in winter. My sister has just finished her exams and my brother has already gone to work. We've always wanted to travel abroad together.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: 've/'s contractions present, 'been' long, and 'ever/never' stressed.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself talking about your life experiences. Then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت تتكلم عن خبراتك في الحياة، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل نقطة.
test_yourself.passage: I've had many interesting experiences in my life. I've been to several cities in Egypt, and I've always loved travelling. Have you ever been to Aswan? It's beautiful. I've tried a lot of different foods, but I've never eaten sushi. My sister has just come back from Turkey, and she's been telling everyone about it. My brother has already visited five countries — he's never afraid to travel alone. So far, I've learnt three languages, and I've recently started a new one. Have you ever studied a language just for fun? I think experiences like these have made my life richer.

sounds_to_check.'ve = /v/: I've had, I've been, I've tried, I've learnt, I've recently
sounds_to_check.'s = /z/ (has): she's been, he's never, she's just come
sounds_to_check.'been' /biːn/ (long): I've been to, have you ever been, she's been telling
sounds_to_check.ever/never stress: have you EVER, I've NEVER, he's NEVER
sounds_to_check.weak 'have' in questions: have you ever been, have you ever studied

scoring_guide.90_100: Contractions clear, 'been' long, questions flow with weak 'have'. Ready for week 11.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, keeping the /v/ buzz and the long 'been'.

for_arabic_speakers: The present perfect always needs its auxiliary — 'I've been', never 'I been'.
'been' has a long vowel (like 'bean'); shortening it to 'bin' changes the word.
've is /v/ (teeth on lip, buzz) — Arabic has no /v/, so practise the buzz.
'ever' and 'never' are stressed; 'have' in questions stays weak.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
